skills.name: Solve absolute value inequalities |x − a| < b and |x − a| > b

note.text:
Think of |x − a| as the distance from x to a.
• |x − a| < b: x is closer than b to a, so a − b < x < a + b. One interval: (a − b, a + b).
• |x − a| > b: x is further than b from a, so x < a − b or x > a + b. Two pieces.
With ≤ or ≥ the ends are included.
Example: |x − 3| ≤ 2 → 1 ≤ x ≤ 5, that is [1, 5]. |x + 1| > 4 → x < −5 or x > 3.
For |ax + b| < c write −c < ax + b < c and solve all three parts.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text:
By the end, you should be able to turn an absolute value inequality into an interval (or two pieces) and show it on a number line.
Builds on: Lesson {17} (absolute value as distance) and Lesson {16} (interval notation).
Leads to: Lesson {19} (quadratic inequalities) and tolerances such as {50} cm ± {2} cm.

sections.heading: Close to a: one interval
sections.text:
|x − {3}| ≤ {2} asks for the numbers at most {2} away from {3}.
Start at {3} and go {2} each way: from {1} to {5}. So {1} ≤ x ≤ {5}, that is {interval(1, 5, true, true)}.
In general |x − a| < b gives a − b < x < a + b: one interval, centre a, half-width b.
With a coefficient, write it as a double inequality: |{poly([2, 'x'], [1, ''])}| < {7} → {-7} < {poly([2, 'x'], [1, ''])} < {7} → {-4} < x < {3}.

sections.heading: Far from a: two pieces
sections.text:
|x + {1}| > {4} means x − ({-1}) is more than {4} from {0}: x is more than {4} away from {-1}.
On the left: x < {-1} − {4} = {-5}. On the right: x > {-1} + {4} = {3}.
So x < {-5} or x > {3}. On a number line this is two arrows pointing away from each other.
A tolerance works the same way: a length of {50} cm ± {2} cm means |L − {50}| ≤ {2}, so {48} ≤ L ≤ {52}.

key_words.meaning: the largest allowed difference from a target value

mistake.why: > means far from the centre: the solutions lie outside the interval, on both sides.

worked_example.problem: Solve |x − {a}| ≤ {k} and write the answer in interval notation.
steps: |x − {a}| ≤ {k} means x is at most {k} away from {a}.

cards.idea: |x| < k means x lies between −k and k.
|x − a| ≤ b: the numbers at most b away from a form one interval [a − b, a + b].
|x − a| > b: the numbers more than b away from a lie on both sides, outside the interval.

misconceptions.explain: That is |x − {br(a)}| < {k}: the numbers close to {a}.
Numbers far away on the left count too: x < {a - k}.
The distance is measured from {a}, not from {0}.

solution: The numbers more than {k} away from {a}: on the left below {a - k}, on the right above {a + k}.

misconceptions.explain: x = {-k - 3} is less than {k}, but |{-k - 3}| = {k + 3} is not less than {k}.
That describes |x| > {k}: the numbers far from {0}.
The sign is <, so ±{k} themselves are left out.

solution: |x| < {k} means x is less than {k} away from {0}.
So x lies between {-k} and {k}, ends left out.

misconceptions.explain: The centre is {a}, not {0}: start from {a} and go {k} each way.
≤ includes the ends, so use square brackets.

solution: The numbers at most {k} away from {a}.

misconceptions.explain: That is |x − {br(a)}| < {k}: the numbers close to {a}.
Numbers far away on the left count too: x < {a - k}.
The distance is measured from {a}, not from {0}.

solution: The numbers more than {k} away from {a}: on the left below {a - k}, on the right above {a + k}.

misconceptions.explain: The sign is <, so {a - k} and {a + k} are left out.
Count both sides of {a}: {k - 1} below, {k - 1} above, and {a} itself.

solution: The whole numbers from {a - k + 1} to {a + k - 1}.

questions.correct: {interval((-c - b) / m, (c - b) / m, true, true)}

distractors.text: {interval((-c + b) / m, (c + b) / m, true, true)}
{intervalIneq('-inf', (-c - b) / m, false, true)} or x ≥ {(c - b) / m}

misconceptions.explain: Take {b} away from every part: {-c} − {br(b)} = {-c - b} and {c} − {br(b)} = {c - b}.
≤ means close to the centre: one interval, not two pieces.

solution: Divide by {m}: {(-c - b) / m} ≤ x ≤ {(c - b) / m}.
